question.text: This man had formerly served as the Collector of the Port of New York before being fired. This successor of James Garfield as president signed the Pendleton Civil Service Act into law.
question.clue: His term in office saw the passage of the Chinese Exclusion Act, and began as a result of the actions of Charles Giteau.

swap.text: This corrupt New York political machine supported many Democratic politicians during the late-19th and early-20th centuries. It was depicted as a ferocious tiger by political cartoonist Thomas Nast.
swap.clue: To gain power as a sachem of this society, "Honest" John Kelly aided Samuel Tilden in fighting this organization's corruption.

question.text: Bryan lost the 1896 Presidential election after being heavily outspent by this man. He was succeeded by Theodore Roosevelt after his 1901 assassination in Buffalo, New York.
question.clue: This president's campaign manager, Mark Hanna, helped create his successful "front porch campaign."

swap.leadin: Eugene Debs was arrested in the aftermath of this event, after which he became a Socialist.
swap.text: Name this railroad strike and boycott that crippled transportation in 1894.
swap.clue: Governor John Atgeld was opposed to the federal response to this event, which occurred after the disruption of the mail service.

question.leadin: This man was the only Admiral of the Navy.
question.text: Name this general who exclaimed "You may fire when ready, Gridley" at the Battle of Manila Bay.
question.clue: This man annihilated the fleet of Patricio Montojo y Pasaron by issuing the order "You may fire when you are ready, Gridley" while on board his flagship, the USS Olympia.

swap.text: This Carnegie steel manager was primarily responsible for handling the Pinkertons. Almost assassinated by Alexander Berkman, this man also owned a whiskey company with Andrew Mellon.
swap.clue: Joseph Duveen advised this man on purchasing works like Vermeer's Officer and Laughing Girl for his Fifth Avenue mansion.

question.leadin: Henry Simpson McComb leaked incriminating letters about this scandal to the New York Sun.
question.text: Name this political scandal, during which George Francis Train and Thomas Durant established a fraudulent railroad construction company and bribed U.S. representatives to cover it up.
question.clue: Peter A. Day was fired for providing ungenerous estimates in this scandal, while James Brooks was censured in the investigation following its exposure.

swap.text: The Knights of Labor took a huge hit after this 1886 Chicago strike of workers because the AFL was soon founded after its occurence. It began after one demonstrator threw a bomb at an officer.
swap.clue: Governor John Altgeld pardoned three men convicted of conspiracy for inciting this event.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the free silver movement per part.
question.text: This 1878 act rectified the "Crime of 73" by resuming recognition of the silver dollar and requiring at least two million dollars of silver to be coined each month.
question.clue: It replaced the "Crime of 1873" and mandated a 16-to-1 ratio after it was passed over the veto of Rutherford B. Hayes, who only complied with the minimum requirements of this law.

swap.leadin: Name these events in military-Native American relations.
swap.text: An 1890 massacre at this South Dakota site was the culmination of the Ghost Dance movement, and it was also the site of a 1973 action by the American Indian Movement.
swap.clue: The Big Foot Memorial Riders end their path at this place, remembering an event that began due to Black Coyote's deafness.

question.text: One of the few lasting achievements of the Arthur administration was this 1883 bill, attempting to end the office-dealing which led to 's assassination, which mandated merit-based federal employment.
question.clue: This 1883 act guaranteed that citizens could compete for federal appointment on the basis of examinations as opposed to the spoils system.

swap.text: This Iowa representative was nominated for president by the Greenback-Labor Party in 1880 and in 1892 by the Populist Party.

question.text: Chicago businessman Montgomery Ward, a competitor of this man, financed early Grange consumer cooperatives in the 1870s. After retiring, this man left his mail-order business to Julius Rosenwald.

swap.text: This Missouri Congressman lost the 1896 Democratic nomination to Bryan after the speech and was chairman of the Committee on Coinage, Weights, and Measures.
swap.clue: American History (Allison) Iowa Senator William Allison revised this Representative's original bill, calling for a monthly limit of $2-4 million worth in silver for coinage purposes.

question.leadin: This event took place in a narrow lot on the side of C. S. Fly's Photographic Studio.
question.text: Name this 30-second event that resulted in the deaths of Tom and Frank McLaury and Billy Clanton.
question.answerHtml: gunfight at the O.K. Corral [or shootout at the O.K. Corral]
question.clue: During this incident, the Clantons, two of the Outlaw Cowboys, fought the interim marshall, Doc Holliday.

swap.text: Shocking stories of adultery in this family surrounded a 1934 custody dispute between Gloria Morgan and Gertrude Whitney over possession of a trust fund after the death of Reginald, the son of Cornelius.
swap.clue: In 1877, a member of this family paid Woodhull $1,000 to leave the country. A railroad tycoon from this family names a university in Nashville.

question.leadin: Answer the following about women who spied for the Union during the American Civil War.
question.text: Sarah E. Edmonds joined the rolls of recipients of these things thanks to an exaggerated memoir of her wartime spying. Grover Cleveland vetoed many expansions of these things promoted by the Grand Army of the Republic.

swap.text: This institution in Upstate New York was founded by Lewis Miller and John Heyl Vincent as a teaching camp for Sunday school teachers. It included Palestine Park, a scale model of the Holy Land.
swap.clue: This institution that names a late 19th-century adult education movement whose lecturers and entertainers, including Russell Conwell, reached 35 million people on its "circuit."

question.text: While this woman was involved with temperance, she was better known for her work with the Populist Party. She is credited with saying "you farmers need to raise less corn and more hell."
question.clue: This Irish-American itinerant orator and staunch supporter of presidential candidate James Weaver. She apocryphally told farmers to "raise less corn and more hell."

swap.leadin: Its preamble was written by Ignatius Donnelly.
swap.text: Identify this set of demands adopted by the Populist Party at the namesake city on July 4th 1892. They include a graduated income tax, the nationalization of railroads and the unlimited coinage of silver.
swap.clue: Many of the Ocala Demands were incorporated into this document, which demanded the direct election of senators and the free and unlimited coinage of silver and gold in a sixteen to one ratio.
